The watery is yellow and whitish: The sapphire-colored, however, is yellow and completely transparent, and has nothing of wateriness, and this is better, as is read in the writings of the sages that, when it is worn on a finger or on the neck, it makes the traveler safe and pleasant to hosts. It also promotes sleep because of its coldness: and the sapphire-colored one has this uniquely.

When you want to be secure from various falls and poisonous bites, then take the stone called <term>orithes</term>: of which there are three kinds: one black, the other green, the third has one part rough and the other smooth: and its color is like an iron plate. And this is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before his death. He said: The Lord came from Sinai and dawned upon them from Seir; He shone forth from Mount Paran, and He came from among ten thousands of holy ones; at His right hand was a fiery law for them. Indeed, He loves the peoples; all His holy ones are in Your hand, and they followed at Your feet, receiving Your words. Moses commanded us a law <term>Torah</term> <gloss>teaching or instruction</gloss>, an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob. And He was King in Jeshurun <note>a poetic name for Israel</note>, when the heads of the people were gathered, the tribes of Israel together.

Let Reuben live and not die, and let his men be few in number. And this for Judah; and he said: Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people; let his hands be sufficient for him, and be a help against his adversaries.

And of Levi he said: Your <term>Thummim</term> and Your <term>Urim</term> <gloss>sacred lots used for divination by the High Priest</gloss> belong to Your pious man, whom You tested at Massah, and with whom You strived at the waters of Meribah; who said of his father and mother, "I have not seen them," and he did not acknowledge his brothers, nor did he know his own children; for they observed Your word and kept Your covenant. They shall teach Your ordinances to Jacob and Your law to Israel; they shall put incense before You and whole burnt offerings upon Your altar. Bless, Lord, his substance, and accept the work of his hands; strike the loins of those who rise against him and of those who hate him, so that they rise no more.

Of Benjamin he said: The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by Him; He covers him all the day long, and He dwells between his shoulders.

And of Joseph he said: Blessed of the Lord be his land, with the precious things of heaven, with the dew, and with the deep that couches beneath; with the precious fruits of the sun, and with the precious yield of the months; with the finest produce of the ancient mountains, and with the precious things of the everlasting hills; with the precious things of the earth and its fullness, and the favor of Him who dwelt in the bush. Let these come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the head of him who was prince among his brothers. His firstborn bull is his glory, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox; with them he shall gore the peoples, all of them, to the ends of the earth; these are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh.

And of Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents. They shall call peoples to the mountain; there they shall offer righteous sacrifices; for they shall suck the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.

And of Gad he said: Blessed is He who enlarges Gad; he dwells like a lioness, and tears the arm, even the crown of the head. He chose the first part for himself, for there the commander's portion was reserved; and he came with the heads of the people; he executed the justice of the Lord and His ordinances with Israel.

And of Dan he said: Dan is a lion's whelp that leaps from Bashan.

And of Naphtali he said: O Naphtali, satisfied with favor, and full of the blessing of the Lord, possess the sea and the south.

And of Asher he said: Blessed be Asher above sons; let him be favored by his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil. Your bolts shall be iron and bronze, and as your days, so shall your strength be.

There is none like God, O Jeshurun, who rides the heavens to help you, and in His majesty through the skies. The eternal God is a dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms; He drove out the enemy before you and said, "Destroy!" So Israel dwells in safety, the fountain of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and wine; His heavens also drop down dew. Happy are you, O Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord, the shield of your help, and the sword of your majesty! Your enemies shall cringe before you, and you shall tread upon their high places.

<column-break/>

Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, which is opposite Jericho. And the Lord showed him all the land: Gilead as far as Dan, all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the Western Sea, the Negeb, and the Plain—that is, the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees—as far as Zoar. And the Lord said to him, "This is the land of which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'I will give it to your offspring.' I have let you see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over there."

So Moses the servant of the Lord died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the Lord. And He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth-peor; but no one knows the place of his burial to this day. Moses was a hundred and twenty years old when he died; his eye was not undimmed, and his vigor had not abated. And the people of Israel wept for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days; then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.

And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him; so the people of Israel obeyed him and did as the Lord had commanded Moses. And there has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face, none like him for all the signs and the wonders that the Lord sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land, and for all the mighty power and all the great terror that Moses performed in the sight of all Israel.

Completed on this Yom Kippur <gloss>Day of Atonement</gloss>, I stood and read to all Israel in my day.
The humble author <note>literally "the small author"</note> erased my perfection <note>or "innocence"</note> to their place <unclear>Amen</unclear>.

Musicians think of breaking the fingers of Bo Ya <note>a legendary master of the zither whose skill aroused envy</note>; charioteers wish to shove aside the hands of Wang Liang <note>a famous charioteer of antiquity</note>. Why is this? It is because they wish to monopolize the reputation for excellence and skill, and loathe seeing others surpass themselves.

For this reason, the beauty from Wei was exquisitely gorgeous, yet Zheng Xiu <note>the jealous consort of King Huai of Chu who deceived the newcomer into covering her nose and then had it cut off</note> had her nose severed; Chao Wu was loyal and steadfast, yet Wu Ji <note>a corrupt minister of Chu who slandered Chao Wu</note> drove him into exile. The afflicted hunchback is intensely jealous, and the deformed cripple is full of flattery <note>allusions to figures in the Classic of Poetry representing petty or resentful courtiers</note>. Therefore, on damp ground in a hall, dust does not scatter; beneath a low roof, the wind cannot be blocked. Things standing directly in the rush of the gale cannot grow to maturity; the banks where water rushes in a torrent cannot maintain steep cliffs.

Under such conditions, the imprisonment at Youli <note>where King Wen of Zhou was detained by the tyrant King Zhou</note> and the distress between Chen and Cai <note>where Confucius and his disciples were besieged and starved</note> can be understood, as can jumping into rivers or drowning in floods <note>as Qu Yuan did when driven to despair by slander</note>. By writing the name called Afumiya today, one sees the seeds of gossip in this fleeting world. The talk of the people in the village, criticizing the young woman of the house <note>original: "里の小かゝ" (sato no kokaka), referring to the daughter or young mistress of the establishment</note> (Baifu of Afumiya), became a struggle. Even the sliding doors at the gate were locked, yet because she would not mingle with those who entered, the depth of the world's malice made her heart bitter. Since she would not refuse them, she became the subject of gossip. A volume titled "Waking from Sleep" <note>original: "寝覚" (Nezame)</note> was circulated, focusing on the rumors surrounding Afumiya. This focus on Afumiya turned to profit, making her famous in the world.

Writing the entrance of the servant girl, with no words to speak, discarding the door behind her, calling it the Age of the Gods <note>original: "神代" (kamiyo), an idiom implying something archaic or long-distant</note>. She was urged to take this letter to Afumiya. Without a suspicious heart, the daughter of Afumiya, the girl of the west, was treated with respect. Remembering the modesty of her words, her mother wrote a letter <note>original: "玉章" (tamazusa), a literary term for a letter</note>. Afumiya took this hidden note to be a matter concerning her family home. She masked the affair, claiming it was nothing but an innocent matter concerning the name Afumiya itself. To speak of it beyond that is sorrowful. The talk of the world, speaking of the mouth of Afumiya, what shall we call it? Until now, it was a thing of the past, a matter regarding the parents of Afumiya.

### Den xxxiiij. Psalm.

David sijnde van een dootlijcke gevaerlijckheyt wonderbaerlijck verlost, vermaent alle geloovigen, na sijn voorschrift, God te loven ende op hem te vertrouwen. Leerende dat het rechte middel van wel salich te wesen, is God te vreesen, welcke alle dingen bestierende, de goddeloosen verdelget, ende de Godsaligen bewaert.

*Een liedt Davids, doe hy sijn gelaet verandert hadde, inde tegenwoordicheyt van Abimelech, die hem verdreef, ende hy ginck wech.*

a black object is black, that by which a thing is such a thing, <term>tode ti</term> <gloss>a "this-something," or a particular individual thing</gloss> ¹. It is the principle by which the substance is in its actual state and not in another state; it is the substance considered as being *in act*, <term>hōs energeia ousia</term> <gloss>substance as actuality</gloss> ².

But the things that we study are subject to change. The object of which we speak can be sometimes black and sometimes white; that is to say that when it has white as its actual tint, it is possible for it to become black; when it is actually black, it is possible for it to become white. At the same time, therefore, that we conceive what it is actually and, consequently, its form, we must conceive what it is in potentiality; and this potentiality to be something else is precisely what remains in the substance while it is actually such a thing; it is by this potentiality that the substance is matter. "I name it matter," says Aristotle ³, "in that it is not actually this thing, but that it is potentially this thing. <term>Hylēn de legō hē mē tode ti ousa energeia dynamei esti tode ti</term>."

Matter is therefore opposed to form as potentiality (<term>dynamis</term>) is opposed to act (<term>energeia</term>). This opposition is the essential character of the Physics of Aristotle.

We have seen that in every substance susceptible to generation, change, and destruction, there is matter; such a substance, indeed, has the potentiality to be what it is not in act; while it is actually such a substance, it is in potentiality to become, through corruption, such another substance; while it is actually in such a state, it is in potentiality to receive such another state.

Is there matter in beings incapable of generation, alteration, and corruption, as the celestial bodies will be, according to the preference of Aristotle? Assuredly, if these substances are susceptible to changing place. Indeed, while such a being is actually in such a place, it is in potentiality to find itself in other places.
